### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **41** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/package.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/package.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **46** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `18fe06b4bfb38a4f1cdcdb4fd628c62d5911ccf1` — the merge of head `f2f8b4ff90786fdb610f103b4b1c7441e82432d0` into base `6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 18fe06b4bfb38a4f1cdcdb4fd628c62d5911ccf1 && git checkout 18fe06b4bfb38a4f1cdcdb4fd628c62d5911ccf1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3 f2f8b4ff90786fdb610f103b4b1c7441e82432d0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3 && git merge --no-ff f2f8b4ff90786fdb610f103b4b1c7441e82432d0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6be71abc34cdd7adcc6057d121479ba5a11724e3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review: E3 #31674, head d8564106 · 2026-11-09T05:28Z**

Verdict: **CHANGES REQUIRED**, on two items, both in `resolvePermissionScoped`'s tail. The rest passes.

**Item 1: a resolved holder that is not servable must not fall through to the metadata service (red lines 1 and 2).**
- When the resolver answers `resolved` but `servable()` rejects the item (most simply, its package is disabled), a caller with no package goes on to `fromMetadata('permission', name)`.
- That is a by-name read. It can hand back the same disabled package's definition, or another body of that name. Either way the registry's one answer has been replaced by a second lookup: a fallback in a permission path.
- Required: once the registry has answered (`resolved` or `refused`), its answer is final. Resolved but not servable is `not-found` and grants nothing.
- `fromMetadata` is consulted only when the registry holds the name nowhere (`not-found`).
- Pin it with a test that is red without the fix: a disabled package's set, with a metadata-service body of that name, read by a caller with no package, grants nothing.

**Item 2 (seat's question 1): a set only the metadata service holds, read by a package caller, is the D3 (a) refusal, not not-found.**
- For a caller with a package, an environment-only holder is refused as `outside-closure`, naming the environment (D3 (a), as R refuses it).
- Answering not-found grants the same nothing, but it hides the holder from the boot report and from the delegated-admin boundary. Red line 2 is "reported, never guessed".
- Required: when `caller !== null`, the registry answers not-found, and `fromMetadata` finds a body, return `refused` (`outside-closure`, candidates: the environment) with R's message. Never serve it.
- Pin it with a test that is red without the fix.

**Passes:**
- **Red line 1:** permission sets resolve through `resolvePackageScopedHolders` and metadata-core's `packageResolutionClosure`. There is no second rule, no second closure, and no injection; the runtime objectql edge is gone. A position's sets resolve from the package that shipped it. Stored grants, environment positions, overlays and `.custom` overrides read as a caller with no package. The audience anchors everyone and guest read caller-less (my reading, recorded). A registry with only part of the slice throws instead of reading half by package.
- **Red line 2:** a refusal grants nothing and names every candidate, in `resolveReference`, in the delegated-admin boundary and in the boot report. Positions are unchanged, and the D7 pin is kept.
- **Red line 3:** (a)–(d) are present. Core gains a runtime dependency on metadata-core, which depends only on spec, so there is no cycle; lean-entry and core-boundary checks are green. The narrowing counts are 0 first-party (HotCRM not measured). Six ablations, 107/107 gates, full dogfood green.
- The census-loader `import.meta.url` shim is accepted. It is tooling, needed by `createRequire`.

**Seat's question 2 (CLI organization-ownership catalog by name):** its own card, not S4. S4 is the upgrade report and bind command. File it as `domain:server`, Part of #31527, Blocked-by #31674.

Send me the head with both items in, and I will re-check only those two. It is not a governed surface.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line re-check: E3 #31674, head f2f8b4ff · 2026-11-09T06:33Z**

Verdict: **PASS.**

Both items from 6732998040 are in:
1. **The registry's answer is final.** A resolved holder that cannot be served is `not-found`, with no by-name `fromMetadata` fallthrough. The metadata service is read only when the registry holds the name nowhere. Pinned with a disabled package plus a same-name metadata body, which gives not-found for every caller; ablation 7 is red.
2. **A metadata-only set read by a package caller is the D3 (a) refusal.** It returns `outside-closure` with candidates `[environment]` and the message from `packageScopedRefusalMessage`. It is never served and never hidden as a miss. A caller with no package is still served it. Pinned, and ablation 8 is red. The `Narrowing:` line now counts this case under D3 (a).

Everything else from the round-1 record stands. CI is green, and core security, plugin-security, 107/107 gates and dogfood (0 refusal lines) all pass. Seat 3 accepts and lands it. It is not a governed surface.

After this lands, S2 #31683 (Blocked-by E3 and E4) is free to leave `pm:blocked`, since E4 is already merged.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #31815 (Fixes #31674, ADR-0150 E3) · 2026-11-09T06:34Z

Head-sha: `f2f8b4ff90786fdb610f103b4b1c7441e82432d0`

- **Form:** draft to `main`. The first content line is `Fixes #31674`, and the whole card lands here. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Skills-docs: follow-up #31819`. The CLI migration catalog is #31817.
- **Premise measured:** core's `security-catalog.ts` resolves a package position's permission sets through R2's `resolvePackageScopedHolders`, over the registry's holder reads and metadata-core's `packageResolutionClosure`. The injected scope, plugin-security's adapter and its runtime objectql edge are removed. Core takes `@objectstack/metadata-core` as a runtime dependency, with no cycle; `check:lean-entry-closure` holds its 15-package set, and `core-boundary.ratchet` is green.
- **Review round 1 (epic 6732998040), both fixed:**
  1. A registry answer, resolved or refused, is final. A resolved holder that may not be served is not-found, with no `fromMetadata` fallthrough. Pin: a disabled package plus a same-named metadata body gives not-found. Ablation 7 goes red.
  2. A set that only the metadata service holds, read by a package caller, gets the D3 (a) `outside-closure` refusal naming the environment, through R's `packageScopedRefusalMessage`. A caller with no package is still served. Ablation 8 goes red.
- **Gates (check-runs on this head):** 70 runs, 58 success, 11 skipped, 1 in progress: `Check Changeset`, re-running after the body patch, which the queue gates. `check-governed-merges --pr 31815`: NOT governed, 1135 changed lines. K = 25 first-parent commits on `main` since the PR base, and a local merge with `main` is clean. dispatch-gates: 107 derived, 107 exit 0. Core security: 1279 passed. plugin-security: 6050 passed, 0 failed. Dogfood: 3654 passed, 0 refusal lines on boot.
- **Narrowing:** D3 (a) is not measurable first-party; outside-closure 0; artifact-sibling 0; HotCRM not measured.
- **Accepted deviations:** `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.mjs`'s loader now hands the module its file URL, because the new core→metadata-core edge reaches `createRequire(import.meta.url)`. There are also forced rig fixes where test rigs had served sets a booted kernel's registry does not serve; each is named in the PR.
- **Epic red-line review:** PASS at this head, re-check of round 1 (record on the PR).
- **Out of scope:** filed #31817 and #31819.
- **Landing:** ready and auto-merge in this stroke. On merge: a landing record on #31674, `pm:dispatched` removed, and the card closed by `Fixes`. S2 #31683 is then unblocked, because E3 and E4 have both landed.
